$comment: Record of the release gate in docs/I18N_POLICY.md, 「リリース前の門」.
One entry per locale per high-risk key, written ONLY after: (1) someone who
was not shown the English back-translated the string, and (2) the author read
that back-translation and confirmed the promise survived.
`source` and `target` are SHA-256 hashes of the exact strings that were
reviewed. gate.test.ts recomputes them, so editing either the English or the
translation afterwards turns the approval stale and fails the build. That is
the point: an approval names a specific pair of strings, not a locale.
`by` records who produced the back-translation. It must not be the session
that wrote the translation — a model checking its own work reproduces its own
misreading. Measured on the es guide pass: 0 of 5 real defects found.
EMPTY IS HONEST. The app shipped twelve machine locales before this gate
existed; none of them has been through it. `pnpm i18n:gate` lists what is
outstanding. Do not backfill entries to make it quiet.
